author: mouse
rule: R10 - state what the ledger will decline before running it. A prediction written after the run is a description.

enumeration.how: one gated `pytest tests/ops` run with ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_CLAIM_LOG set; every record whose decline codes are exactly {unproven}
enumeration.not_from: the claim table's enumeration - that shape makes criterion 11 true by construction

predictions.claim: The exact-arithmetic f32 unaries prove cleanly: Abs, Neg, Sign, Floor, Ceil, Round, Identity, Reciprocal. No rounding is involved beyond IEEE, so worst_rel should be 0.0 or denormal-small.
The transcendental f32 unaries prove at rtol=1e-3: Exp, Log, Erf, Sigmoid, Tanh, Gelu, Mish, Softplus, the trig and hyperbolic family. GLSL built-ins and the CPU EP agree far inside 1e-3 at f32.

AT LEAST ONE f16 form will come back DIVERGENT at atol=1e-5, and it will be a transcendental one (Erf, Gelu or Tanh at f16), because f16 machine epsilon is ~9.8e-4 - two orders of magnitude LARGER than the atol - so any difference in the order of operations exceeds the tolerance. If this happens it is a finding about the tolerance's applicability to f16, not about the kernel, and the form stays OUT of the ledger.

GroupQueryAttention will NOT be proven this round. It has 7 inputs and 3 outputs including in-place KV-cache updates, and a one-node case model that feeds it correctly is not a small piece of work. It will be reported as unproven with a reason, not quietly omitted.

Clip's suite failure is NOT fixed by a ledger entry. The claim log shows `[arity] Clip has 1 inputs; this handler takes exactly 3` - a different code from `[unproven]`. A proof of the 3-input form leaves the 1-input form declining for the same reason it declines now. This is a coverage gap, not a proof gap.
Some enumerated keys will produce `unproven_only: 0` at discovery - the form declines for a second reason as well, so proving it changes nothing. Those get no entry and are reported.

The suite will NOT go to 0 failures. Forms declining for [staged], [dtype], [attribute], [opset] and [arity] reasons are unaffected by the ledger, and the claim log counted 87 such records against 765 unproven ones.

Every entry written will carry claimed_nodes > 0 and dispatches_executed > 0, because the generator raises rather than writing an unattributed entry. If a proof run falls back to CPU the verdict is UNATTRIBUTED and no entry appears - the count of entries can therefore go DOWN relative to the number of keys attempted, and that is the mechanism working.

will_not_do: Relax Guard D to reduce the failure count.
Derive any entry from the claim table's enumeration.
Widen rtol/atol to make a DIVERGENT form pass. A tolerance chosen after seeing the number it must admit is not a tolerance.

Quote any timing figure: gpu_steady_tail detects foreign work only through non-stationarity, six agents are on this machine, and no duration is certifiable right now. worst_rel against a CPU oracle needs no clock.
